text:
maria: Quick thread — proposal to reconcile cost/latency/region into a single "blended" decision in the policy engine so runtimes get a ranked list of routes instead of a single black-box choice.

sam: tl;dr: what's the RPC contract change you're imagining?

maria: minimal change: Resolve(RouteRequest) => RouteCandidates where each candidate = {route_id, score, cost_estimate, latency_p50/95, region, compatible_models, provenance_tags}. runtime can pick first compatible candidate or apply local tie-breakers.

jen: need deterministic tie-breaker for canary traffic. otherwise we can't stable-route small % to new stacks. maybe include a stable_seed in request that runtime uses for consistent sorting. :thinking_face:

ashok: perf concern: sending full score_breakdown for every request will blow CPU and network for high qps tenants. Can we support a compact form + optional verbose flag? e.g., a bitset provenance and compressed histograms.

kevin: also need telemetry hooks. every resolved candidate should carry a small explainability blob so Console can show why route X was chosen (or why fallback occurred). This can be sampled to 0.1% by default.

maria: agreed on compactness. API sketch:

```
message RouteRequest {
  string tenant_id = 1;
  int32 max_candidates = 2; // runtime hint, default 3
  bool verbose = 3; // opt-in explainability
  bytes stable_seed = 4; // optional, for deterministic tie-breaks
  map<string,string> constraints = 5; // e.g. {region: eu, max_cost: 0.002}
}

message RouteCandidate {
  string route_id = 1;
  float score = 2; // normalized composite score (higher better)
  float cost = 3;
  float latency_p95 = 4;
  repeated string tags = 5; // small list for provenance
  bytes compact_explain = 6; // optional gzip'd proto when verbose
}
```

sam: nice. does score mean we pre-normalize across regions / gpu-types? that's tricky.

maria: score must be cost-normalized to be comparable across heterogeneous backends. proposal: per-tenant weight vector + device-normalization table maintained by optimizer. Runtime will store the device normalization table, updated via snapshot.

jen: what's fallback semantics if top candidate is overloaded mid-request? Do we let runtime try next candidate or surface error and let client re-resolve?

ashok: runtime should attempt transparent hedging to next candidate for idempotent requests. For non-idempotent, return a structured error that includes next best candidate so clients can decide.

kevin: multi-region traffic: include region_affinity tag and a region_penalty field so Console can show why eu route got lower rank than us-east (e.g., latency penalty + cost credit).

policy-bot: RFC: https://r/infra/policy-blend (draft) — left comments on determinism + sampling.

maria: open questions we need to resolve before RFC:
- max_candidates default (3 vs 5)
- verbose explainability cost/ops
- stable_seed shape and how canaries pass it (sampled header?)
- format for device-normalization snapshots

sam: i'll spin up a sim harness to validate candidate lists + stable_seed determinism. volunteering to own the sim.

jen: i'll draft deterministic tie-break rules and a small test harness for canary % consistency.

ashok: i'll prototype compact_explain encoding (protobuf + gzip) and measure p50 serialization time. I think we can keep 3 candidates w/ compact explains sampled at 0.1% without notable overhead.

kevin: i'll add telemetry metrics we need: candidate_list_size, chosen_candidate_latency, chosen_candidate_cost_estimate, explain_sampled_count, deterministic_mismatch_count.

maria: cool. rollout plan: feature flag in policy compiler + runtime opt-in to return candidates. start with internal tenants and a small canary group. Sam, can you propose a phased rollout checklist?

sam: yes — will post a short checklist. items: sim pass, perf bench, telemetry config, console display stub, canary runbook.

jen: one more: add a "compatibility_score" per-candidate so client-side glue (e.g., when a customer pins a model) can enforce strict compatibility.

maria: perfect. action owners: sam(sim + rollout), jen(tie-break tests), ashok(compact explain), kevin(telemetry), maria(RFC updates + rollout coordination). I'll attach RFC PR after this thread. :white_check_mark:

sam: ack.

ashok: ack.

jen: ack.

kevin: ack.

policy-bot: Noted: RFC draft created, reviewers: @maria @sam @jen @ashok @kevin

maria: Thanks everyone — wrapping up here. We'll track follow-ups in the RFC and a short design doc in /docs/policy-blend.
